newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas up again in winter, volumes remain high.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas up again in winter, volumes remain high.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures continued their recent resurgence on Monday afternoon as 250 lots were traded, of which 175 were done in the afternoon session.
A total of nine deals were done, with all trade confined to the coming winter.
Deals were done in November, December, January and February, but December was the most active month, with 125 lots or half the total trading in this period.

November saw the biggest gains, trading finally at 13.60 pence a therm, an increase of 0.125 pence. But December was also strong, trading four times at 15.30 pence, up by 0.10 pence. Only January saw a slippage, and then only by 0.025 pence a therm, to trade at 18.05 pence.

By the close, front month August was offered at 9.90 pence but not bid. September was also offered at 9.90 pence with a bid at 9.65 pence. Only the eight months from September to April saw both bids and offers.
The relatively high volume followed a busy week last week, when 1475 lots or an average 295 lots a day traded.
